successors.name: Ethiopian Empire
successors.text: the Hadiya country, "eight days' journey by nine" (about 160 by 180 km) in the mid-14th century

ledger.x: 1316: Amda Seyon brings Hadiya under Ethiopian control.
1893: the last Hadiya Muslim polity ends under Menelik II.

wars.name: Amda Seyon's Hadiya campaigns
wars.outcome: After conquering Damot, Amda Seyon "brought Hadiya under his control"; King Amano refused submission and the emperor "slew the inhabitants of the country with the point of the sword".

wars.name: Hadiya revolts against Ethiopia
wars.outcome: Sarsa Dengel suppressed a revolt of Garad Aze at the Battle of Hadiya (1569); in the 1600s Garad Sidi Mohammed defeated Susenyos I's troops, "protecting the frontier for about three centuries".

wars.name: Abyssinian conquest of Hadiya
wars.outcome: Qabeena capitulated in 1875, its resistance under Garad Hassan Enjamo ended at Jabdu Meda in 1889, and the Halaba fell in 1893.

certainty.note: Described by days of travel; no frontier is given.
